lesson_text: Fill me now, at the best price there. That's all a market order says. It almost always fills, as long as there are buyers and sellers. What it doesn't promise is the price. You can get filled away from the quote you saw, most of all when a stock is moving fast. That's the deal, and we take it on every entry. When the setup triggers, I want to be in. A market order buys you the fill. It doesn't buy you the price.

Day orders expire at the end of the trading day; GTC orders stay in effect until they fill or you cancel them. Unless you choose otherwise, an order is a day order, good only for the day you enter it. An immediate-or-cancel (IOC) order fills what it can right away and cancels the rest. At Schwab, extended-hours orders must be limit orders; stop orders are not accepted there. Every position we hold has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in our head.

facts.given: You buy a breakout and plan to hold it for weeks. You're setting the bracket's exits. Which time in force do they need? Good-'til-canceled (GTC) Day, the usual default Immediate-or-cancel (IOC) Extended-hours session

reveal_json.lesson_line: Holding for weeks means GTC exits. A day stop is gone at the close.
reveal_json.simple: Use GTC, because a day order is gone at the close and you'd be holding with no stop.
reveal_json.why: GTC. You're holding for weeks, so the stop has to be there every one of those days. A day order that hasn't filled cancels at the close. Set your exits as day orders and tomorrow morning you're holding a position with no stop. That's the trap, because day is what you get unless you change it. GTC lasts until it fills or you cancel it, up to your broker's limit. Every position we hold has a real stop sitting with the broker.

wrong.Day, the usual default: Day is what you get unless you pick something else. Unfilled, it cancels at the close, and your stop is gone overnight.
wrong.Extended-hours session: That covers the hours around one session, not weeks. Schwab won't even take a stop order there.
wrong.Immediate-or-cancel (IOC): IOC fills what it can right away and cancels the rest. An exit has to sit and wait for its price.

sources.quote: A gap against the stop: the first 30 minutes of the gap-down day decide. The low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop. … With a ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out. … The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule (B20).

depth.summary: When a stock gaps down through our stop, the low of the first 30-minute bar becomes the new stop. If the first 30 minutes of the gap day already put the loss past 2R, we get out. Our stop only moves up, never down or wider; the gap rule is the one exception.

facts.given: Your stock gaps down through your stop at the open. The low of the first 30-minute bar becomes your new stop.

reveal_json.lesson_line: Gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low is the new stop. Past 2R, you're out.
reveal_json.simple: True. On a gap through your stop, the first 30 minutes decide, and their low is your new stop.
reveal_json.why: True. That's our gap rule. Rather than dump it into the opening panic, you let the first 30 minutes show you where it holds. Their low becomes the new stop. There's a ceiling: if those 30 minutes already put the loss past 2R, you get out. It's the one time a stop moves down. Every other time it only moves up.
